## Nothing appears — that's the finding

The second `S` succeeds. You get a second address space, same jobname, different ASID, and no message anywhere saying "already running."

The start-up messages just repeat, identically. Which pair depends on how you start it:

- **`SUB=MSTR`** (likely, if your server registers in the SSI — subsystems usually can't wait for JES): `IEF695I START <proc> WITH JOBNAME <n> IS ASSIGNED TO USER…` followed by `IEF403I <n> - STARTED - TIME=…`. No `$HASP` messages at all.
- **Under JES2**: `$HASP373 <n> STARTED` plus the `IEF403I`.

Confirm it in ten seconds with `D A,<n>` — if you get two entries with different ASIDs, the second copy is up and your check did not stop it.

**Why nothing blocks it:** JES2's duplicate-jobname protection (`DUPL_JOB=DELAY` on `JOBDEF`/`JOBCLASS`) is scoped to *batch jobs*. STCs and TSU are outside it entirely, and a `SUB=MSTR` task never goes near JES2 in the first place. The clinching evidence is `IEE824I DUPLICATE NAME FOUND - REENTER COMMAND WITH 'A=' KEYWORD`: that `A=` keyword on `P`/`F`/`C` exists *because* same-named address spaces are expected to coexist. If z/OS rejected the second START, the keyword would have nothing to disambiguate.

So the first visible symptom typically isn't at START time at all — it's the next time someone issues `P <n>` or `F <n>` and gets `IEE824I` instead of the action they wanted.

## Why your own check is silent

Two candidate causes, different in kind. I can't pick between them without your registration code.

**Mundane:** the WTO isn't reaching a console — no `ROUTCDE`/`DESC` coded (so it lands in the joblog/SYSLOG only), MPF suppression, or the message is going to JESMSGLG/SYSPRINT rather than out as a WTO.

**Structural — I'd chase this one first.** The check tests the wrong thing and the program falls through. `IEFSSVT REQUEST=CREATE` does *not* fail merely because copy 1 already created one; a subsystem is permitted multiple SSVTs, and the subsequent `EXCHANGE` then succeeds too. Only the `IEFSSI REQUEST=ADD` returns nonzero name-already-defined. A program that doesn't test that return code — or tests it but whose failure path doesn't terminate — walks straight into CREATE + EXCHANGE and **silently takes over copy 1's registration**. No error, no message. That fits "never seems to produce a message" better than the WTO theory does.

The concrete thing to check: is the `IEFSSI ADD` return code tested, and does its failure path actually terminate, or does it fall through to CREATE/EXCHANGE? (I've deliberately not quoted specific return/reason code values — IBM's docs 403'd me. The exact codes are in *MVS Using the Subsystem Interface*.)

## The hazard this is hiding

After that EXCHANGE, the SSCT points at copy 2's SSVT and function routines. SSI function routines get control in the **caller's** address space, so everything they touch must be in common storage. When copy 1 is later stopped and frees its ECSA SSVT and routines, SSI callers can start taking `0C4`s in unrelated address spaces — long after, and with nothing pointing back at the duplicate START.

**Recommendation:** serialize with an exclusive `ENQ` on a private QNAME before you touch the SSI at all. Second copy fails the ENQ, issues its WTO, terminates. That's the standard idiom and it doesn't depend on getting SSI return codes exactly right.

If you paste the registration path, I'll tell you which of the two causes you have.

Sources: [JES2 duplicate job name control](https://www.ibm.com/docs/SSLTBW_2.4.0/com.ibm.zos.v2r4.hasa300/dupjob.htm) · [JES2 duplicate job names](https://www.ibm.com/docs/SSLTBW_2.2.0/com.ibm.zos.v2r2.hasa300/has2v5_Duplicate_job_names.htm) · [Controlling JES2 initiators](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/2.4.0?topic=execution-controlling-jes2-initiators) · [IEE messages (IEE700I–IEE892I)](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/2.4.0?topic=iee-messages-iee700i-iee892i)
